title: Orchestration: deterministic replay validator & jitter-mitigation for CUDA-graph multi-stream decode
creator: Ava Patel
description: Problem: Intermittent divergence and rare non-deterministic failures during CUDA-graph capture/replay when running multi-stream decode with overlapping prefill + decode workloads. Failures manifest as token mismatches or out-of-order KV cache states in production traces; they are hard to reproduce locally because they depend on timing jitter across streams, kernel launch ordering, and rare race windows during graph capture. Background: existing tickets have focused on capture safety and replay correctness, but we still see live incidents where an otherwise nominal workload hits a scheduling jitter window and produces a mismatched output. Goal: implement an orchestration layer and deterministic replay validator that (1) gates asynchronous captures with a light-weight alignment protocol, (2) detects and mitigates jitter windows by delaying capture or falling back to safe-path synchronous capture, and (3) provides automated shadow-replay validation that compares outputs (and KV-cache deltas) to a golden baseline to detect regressions early in CI and can be run against production traces for postmortems.
acceptance_criteria: 1) No regression in throughput or P95 latency beyond agreed threshold (<3% P95 increase) when enabling mitigation in Canary. 2) Shadow-replay tool runs end-to-end on nightly golden prompt suites and flags divergence automatically. 3) For 10k sample live requests replayed in staging, divergence rate must be < 0.001%. 4) Rollback path: if gated capture detects jitter, system falls back deterministically to safe capture path with observable metric and alert emitted. 5) Documentation describing new gating protocol, operator runbook, and runbook for investigating replay flags.
plan: Phase 1: Design and prototype (this ticket) - refine lightweight capture gate protocol, implement deterministic token-marker alignment, add instrumentation hooks to capture KV-delta snapshots. Phase 2: Implement shadow-replay validator as a separate binary that can read trace blobs and compare outputs with configurable tolerance. Phase 3: Canary rollout with runtime flag and telemetry; run golden-suite nightly. Phase 4: Production rollout + automation for auto-retry/backoff when jitter detected. Implementation tasks: - add capture-gate state machine in runtime (align-start, mark-token, capture, tag-graph) - implement jitter detector using micro-timestamps and kernel-cost window estimates - add synchronous safe-path fallback and metric emission - build replay-checker service and CI integration - add end-to-end system tests simulating stream jitter and kernel preemption
tests: Unit tests for capture-gate state transitions; fuzz harness that injects artificial stream jitter and kernel delays; deterministic golden-suite with 500 prompts covering short/long prefill and multi-turn decode; integration test that runs shadow-replay on recorded staging traces and asserts KV-cache equivalence within bit-tolerance; performance benchmark comparing throughput/latency with gating enabled vs disabled on p4d and a100 nodes.
risks: 1) Performance regressions if gating is too conservative; mitigate with micro-benchmarks and adjustable thresholds. 2) False positives from replay-checker due to non-deterministic ops (floating point noise, async cuBLAS scheduling) — address with tolerances and kernel-agnostic comparison of token-level outputs and KV checksums. 3) Complexity added to runtime state machine increasing maintenance burden. 4) Long tail edge-cases where fallback may increase latency — expose as opt-in per-customer config.
